clue.text: Even so, no fool has hard reputation

parts.note: taken as written
a twit is a fool
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
standing is one's reputation or status

explanation.surface: Someone is told that, all the same, a person who is no fool has a tough name to live up to.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no fool' looks like one idea, but NO and TWIT are separate pieces; 'has' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are concessive expressions meaning in spite of that or nevertheless.

clue.text: Stand to look at stage

parts.note: to view something is to look at it
a point is a stage reached, as in 'at this point'

explanation.surface: An instruction to stand somewhere in order to look at the stage of a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A stand is a position taken on an issue, a synonym of a point of view.

clue.text: Mixed batter British rejected for fish

indicators.note: batter that is mixed has its contents stirred about, so the remaining letters are rearranged
British is rejected, so its letter is thrown out of the word batter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook mixes a batter, rejects the British method, and serves fish.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing B from BATTER leaves ATTER, which 'Mixed' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Depressingly dull back in outskirts of Derby

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the outer letters of the town name
the outskirts of a town are its edges, so take the first and last letters of Derby

parts.note: the rear is the back

explanation.surface: A gloomy description of the back streets on the edge of the English city of Derby.
explanation.walkthrough: The outskirts of Derby are D and Y, which go round REAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Dreary is a synonym of depressingly dull, bleak and tedious.

clue.text: Rough husband destroyed an igloo

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for husband in family trees

indicators.note: an igloo that is destroyed has its blocks scattered, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A husband has smashed up an igloo, a rough act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rough' looks like an adjective, but it is a noun here: a rough is a thug.
explanation.definitionFit: A rough is a violent troublemaker, a synonym of a thug or yob.

clue.text: Invader stripped land, after the usual thing

indicators.note: the stripped word follows the other piece

parts.note: the norm is the usual state of affairs

indicators.note: a word stripped loses its outer layer, so drop the first and last letters of land

explanation.surface: An invader stripped the land bare, as invaders usually do.
explanation.definitionFit: The Normans invaded England in 1066, so one of them is a classic invader.

clue.text: Berate salesman introducing insect pest

indicators.note: the salesman comes first, introducing the next piece

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
a roach, short for cockroach, is an insect pest

explanation.surface: Someone tells off a salesman who has brought in cockroaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To reproach someone is to scold or rebuke them, a synonym of berate.

clue.text: Protest note over reduction in status

parts.note: a demo is a protest march
ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
on can mean over, as in a lid on a pot

explanation.surface: A protest note is lodged about someone's downgrading.
explanation.definitionFit: A demotion is a lowering of rank, a reduction in status.

clue.text: Team members remain without new period of success

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: to lie is to remain, as snow lies
an up is a good spell, as in ups and downs

explanation.surface: Team members stay put while lacking a new run of good form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like 'lacking' but means outside: LIE goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: A line-up is the list of players picked for a team.

clue.text: Infatuated with finest editor introducing some good books

indicators.note: something introduced is put inside, so one piece goes into another

parts.note: best means finest
OT is the Old Testament, part of the Good Book

explanation.surface: An editor is besotted with the finest of literature and slips in some good books.
explanation.walkthrough: BEST takes in OT to give BESOTT, then ED is added.
explanation.definitionFit: Besotted means smitten or infatuated, overwhelmed by love.

clue.text: Live as a prisoner as a warning

parts.note: to be is to live or exist
a con is a convict, a prisoner

explanation.surface: A person lives as a prisoner as a warning to others.
explanation.definitionFit: A beacon is a signal fire lit to warn of danger.

clue.text: Offender's first fine is suspended

indicators.note: the first of the offender is its opening letter

parts.note: nice can mean fine or good

explanation.surface: An offender's first fine is suspended, a lenient sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Something put on ice is held in reserve, suspended for later.

clue.text: Record belonging to us source of excited conversation

parts.note: a disc is a record
ours means belonging to us

indicators.note: the source of a word is where it starts, its first letter

explanation.surface: A record of ours proves the source of excited chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Discourse is talk or conversation between people.

clue.text: Safe natural sand is moving in area of instability

indicators.note: sand that is moving shifts about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Natural sand, once safe, starts shifting in an unstable area.
explanation.definitionFit: The San Andreas Fault in California is a famous earthquake zone where plates grind past each other.

clue.text: In the US, nothing venerable arises from Las Vegas?

indicators.note: in a down clue something that arises reads upwards, so the pieces are reversed

parts.note: nada is a slang word for nothing, from Spanish, used in the US
Ven is the abbreviation for Venerable, an archdeacon's title

explanation.surface: Something old and grand comes out of nothing in Las Vegas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the US' marks NADA as American slang; NADAVEN read upwards gives the answer. The question mark warns that Las Vegas is only one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A person from Las Vegas is a native of the state of Nevada.

clue.text: Article on the beginnings of Middle Eastern melody

parts.note: the is the definite article

indicators.note: the beginnings of the words are their first letters

explanation.surface: A newspaper article on the roots of Middle Eastern music.
explanation.definitionFit: A theme is a main tune or melody in a piece of music.

clue.text: Bring insect into the country in material

parts.note: with 'into the country', to bring goods in from abroad is to import them
an ant is an insect

explanation.surface: Someone brings an insect into the country in some material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bring ... into the country' together means import; 'material' means relevant, as in a material fact.
explanation.definitionFit: A material point is one that matters, an important one.

clue.text: A very small quantity of hydrogen and atmospheric gases

parts.note: H is the chemical symbol for hydrogen
air is the mixture of gases in the atmosphere

explanation.surface: A tiny amount of hydrogen mixed with the air.
explanation.definitionFit: A hair, as in winning by a hair, is a tiny amount or margin.

clue.text: One working with needle to treat drunk with oxygen

indicators.note: something drunk staggers about, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
O is the chemical symbol for oxygen

explanation.surface: A nurse uses a needle to treat a drunk with oxygen.
explanation.definitionFit: A tattooist works with a needle to ink designs on skin.

clue.text: Disastrous having name given for female at birth

indicators.note: one letter given in exchange for another means a swap

parts.note: fatal can mean disastrous, as in a fatal mistake

explanation.surface: Something disastrous happens when a name meant for a girl is given at birth.
explanation.walkthrough: FATAL with N in place of F.
explanation.definitionFit: Natal means relating to birth, as in antenatal.

clue.text: English aim with Northern Ireland all over is to unify

indicators.note: turned all over, so the run of pieces is reversed

parts.note: a target is an aim

explanation.surface: England's aim, with Northern Ireland, is to unite the whole country.
explanation.walkthrough: ETARGETNI read backwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To integrate is to combine parts into a whole, to unify.

clue.text: What's rung badly about a church to make an awful noise

indicators.note: one piece goes round another
rung badly means jumbled, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A peal of bells rung badly in a church makes a terrible noise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'badly' makes GRUN, which 'about' wraps round A. Graunch is a mainly British word for a grinding or crunching noise.
explanation.definitionFit: To graunch is to make a harsh grinding or crunching noise, as gears do.

clue.text: Reduction of charge concerning calling abroad?

parts.note: re means concerning or about
a mission is a vocation, often to work overseas

explanation.surface: A missionary's calling abroad leads to a cut in the fee.
explanation.definitionFit: Remission is the cancellation of a debt or penalty, a reduction of what is charged.

clue.text: Cancelled precipitately?

parts.note: precipitately hints at precipitation: an event called off because of the weather

explanation.surface: Something was called off in a great hurry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'precipitately' looks like 'hastily', but the pun is on rain as precipitation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket match or fete abandoned because of rain is said to be called off by the weather.

clue.text: Bullfighter ripped open: a doctor must cross ring

parts.note: tore means ripped, as in tore open

indicators.note: the ring is crossed, so the doctor's letters span it

parts.note: O is ring-shaped

explanation.surface: A gored bullfighter needs a doctor to come across the bullring.
explanation.walkthrough: DR goes round O to give DOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A toreador is a bullfighter, especially one on horseback.

clue.text: Call one old American untrustworthy

parts.note: to dub is to name or call
I is the Roman numeral for one
US stands for the United States, so American

explanation.surface: Someone labels an old American as unreliable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dubious means doubtful or questionable, hence not to be trusted.

clue.text: Penetrating word play information takes time

parts.note: a pun is a play on words
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: Sharp wordplay takes time to digest.
explanation.definitionFit: A pungent smell or remark is sharp and piercing, that is, penetrating.

clue.text: Something associated with film, say, that is kept in can

indicators.note: one piece is kept inside the other

parts.note: a tin is a can
ie is the abbreviation for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A film is kept in a can, as reels are.
explanation.definitionFit: A tie-in is merchandise or a book linked to a film or show.

clue.text: Running up short dress acceptable for Greek island

indicators.note: in a down clue running up means reading from bottom to top, so the piece is reversed
short means cut off at the end, so the last letter goes

parts.note: a frock is a dress
U means upper-class, hence socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A dressmaker runs up a short dress that is suitable for a Greek island holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: FROCK cut short is FROC, reversed to CORF. 'Running up' also suggests sewing quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is an island in the Ionian Sea belonging to Greece.

clue.text: Landmass like island on top of Australia

parts.note: as means like, as in 'as good as gold'
A is the international vehicle code for Australia

explanation.surface: A landmass looks like an island sitting on top of Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a vast landmass.
